classification.difficultyReason: Read a frequency graph and compare its approximate proportions with alternative spinner geometries.

inlines.text: A spinner can land in any of 4 sections, labelled 1 to 4.
The spinner is spun 100 times and the results are recorded in the bar chart below.
Which of these spinners is most likely to give results shown in the graph?

spec.description: Unfilled bars at 8, 17, 51 and 24; categories 1–4; horizontal grid at 20, 40 and 60.
spec.mathematics: Frequencies total 100. Axis scale and bar heights encode the given counts.
spec.answerVisibility: All chart data are permanent student givens.

spec.description: Unlabelled choice with narrow upper sectors 1 and 2, diagonal diameter, lower-right semicircle 3 and upper-left sector 4.
spec.mathematics: Angles are visual reconstruction parameters, not printed givens.

spec.description: Horizontal diameter; upper-left quarter labelled 4; upper-right quarter split into 1 and 2; lower semicircle labelled 3.
spec.mathematics: Drawn sector proportions approximately 1/8, 1/8, 1/2 and 1/4; no numerical angles printed.

spec.description: Four unfilled quadrants labelled 1, 2, 3, 4 clockwise from upper right.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal and vertical diameters; no angle annotations.

spec.description: Small upper sectors 1 and 2, broad bottom sector 3 exceeding a semicircle, and upper-left sector 4.
spec.mathematics: Boundary directions are visual reconstruction parameters only.

spec.description: Unfilled native selection oval under its spinner; no added option letter.
Unfilled native selection oval under its spinner; no added option letter.
Unfilled native selection oval under its spinner; no added option letter.
Unfilled native selection oval under its spinner; no added option letter.

answer.short: The second spinner from the left.
answer.worked: The relative frequencies of sections 3 and 4 are $\frac{51}{100}\approx\frac12$ and $\frac{24}{100}\approx\frac14$. The second spinner has a lower semicircle labelled 3 and an upper-left quarter labelled 4. Correct answer: the second spinner from the left.
